// Silly Sand Sim by pritzza
// https://www.shadertoy.com/view/X3KcRV

/*
 *  A falling sand simulation cellular automata inspired by 
 *  gelami's falling sand work (https://www.shadertoy.com/view/msBSWK)
 *
 *  Controls:
 *      Num Key (Hold) + Left Click: Place material 
 *      Space: Clear
 *      
 *      Check out "Common" tab to get rid of the border and more
 *
 *  The rules for the cellular automata were designed by me and lack lots of physical rigor (lol). 
 *  In hopes of creating a simple but flexible system with emergent behavior, 
 *  every material is parameterized using only 3 values:
 *    "Density", "Roughness", and "Grainularity".
 *   
 *  Rules:
 *
 *  1) If two materials are slippery enough and grainular enough, they have the chance
 *     to vertically diffuse through eachother each frame. 
 *   
 *     Eg: A water cell ontop of an air cell are allowed to pass through eachother
 *         A sand cell ontop of a helium cell are allowed to pass through eachother
 *         A bark cell ontop of an ice cell cannot pass through eachother
 *       
 *  2) If two materials fail to pass through eachother, one can horizontally slide
 *     another if there isnt much friction between the two and their grainularity allows it.
 *   
 *     Eg: Ice is slippery so a bark cell ontop of ice will slip around
 *      
 *  3) Finally, materials can interact with eachother to form new materials.
 *   
 *     Eg: Lots of fog together has the chance to percipitate into some air and a little bit of water
 *         (More interactions to come!)
 *
 *  Material Controls:
 *      Null: Default
 *      0:    Helium
 *      1:    Air
 *      2:    Fog
 *      3:    Oil
 *      4:    Water
 *      5:    Honey
 *      6:    Mercury
 *      7:    Bark
 *      8:    Sand
 *      9:    Stone
 *
 *  Look in "Common" for all materials.
 */


void mainImage(out vec4 fragColor, in vec2 fragCoord)
{
    // transform camera
    float zoom = ZOOM_VALUE;
    vec2 offset = vec2(X_OFFSET_VALUE, Y_OFFSET_VALUE);
    
    float invertedY = iResolution.y - fragCoord.y - 1.0;
    
    ivec2 coord = ivec2(
        (fragCoord.x - offset.x) / zoom,
        (invertedY   - offset.y) / zoom
    );
    
    // draw cell
    int cellID = coordToID(iChannel0, coord);
    fragColor  = getCellColor(cellID);
}
